title: i18n: validation and refusal messages read field, option and object labels through t(), so a declared i18n.sourceLocale request still names the field with the defaultLocale row
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQjrEpxMVxEiDUJHqC

Found by the contract review of PR #34025 (card #33634, record https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/34025#issuecomment-6897767543, nit N1). It is pre-existing and outside that diff, so it is filed here instead of being fixed there.

**What #33634 fixed.** The five readers that build resolver options (`metaTranslateOptions` in rest, objectql `readerOptionLabels`, plugin-email `servedOptionFields`, analytics `translateSelectOptions`, storage `labelsIn`) now treat `i18n.sourceLocale` as the authored label's language.

**What it did not reach.** A second class of label readers goes through `II18nService.t()`, not through `ResolveOptions`:
- objectql `resolveFieldLabel` (`validation/record-validator.ts`)
- `resolveOptionLabel` (`validation/rule-validator.ts`)
- `objectDisplayLabel` (`engine-validation-messages.ts`)
- their users in `duplicate-record-error.ts` and `engine-delete-cascade.ts`

The reviewer read this in the tree and did not run it. In #33634's scenario (`defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'`, `sourceLocale: 'en'`, no `fallbackLocale`), `t('objects.X.fields.Y.label', 'en')` misses in `en`, falls to the collapsed fallback `zh-CN`, and returns the zh-CN row ahead of the declared English label. So an `en` write refusal still names the field in Chinese.

**Why it matters.** Two sentences shipped by PR #34025 hold for metadata reads, formula `label()`, email option holes, analytics and the upload-link page, but not for validation and refusal messages:
- the `TranslationConfigSchema.sourceLocale` `.describe` text, "a request in this locale is answered from the inline text";
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`, "what the gate counts as covered is what gets served".

**Ask.** Choose one of two routes and implement it:
- (A) The `t()`-based label readers move to the resolver path, building options the way the five readers above do.
- (B) `t()` learns the authored language for metadata label keys.

The #33634 contract deliberately keeps `t()` unchanged ("the value changes no `t()` lookup" in `contracts/i18n-service.ts`). So (B) re-opens that sentence; (A) does not. Seat reading: (A), because it keeps one rule for "which language is the inline label" in one place. Pin the scenario above with an `en` write refusal.

Prior rulings read: #33634's claims and its contract review. Dedupe: open-issue searches for `sourceLocale` and `resolveFieldLabel` found only #33634 itself.
